mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 8 Series 840Ci engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 8 Series 840Ci engine replacement typically costs £1,200-£2,200 for a used M60B40 or M62B44 unit, £2,200-£3,800 for a reconditioned engine, and £3,000-£5,000 for a fully rebuilt engine with warranty. Supply & fit adds £650-£910 in specialist labour (10-14 hours). Used engines offer the lowest upfront cost with limited warranty; reconditioned engines sit in the mid-range with some new parts fitted; rebuilt engines are the most expensive but fully restored to factory spec with a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain tensioner failure in a BMW 840Ci (M60B40)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a rattling or grinding noise from the front of the engine on cold startup, rough idle, and reduced performance. In advanced cases, the engine may misfire or show timing-related fault codes. If you hear a rattle, have the tensioner inspected immediately - a failed tensioner can allow the chain to slip, causing catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 8 Series 840Ci?

acceptedAnswer.text: With average values of £5,000-£15,000, a full rebuilt engine at £3,000-£5,000 represents 20-60% of the vehicle's value. For well-maintained examples worth £10,000+, a rebuilt engine can be a sound investment that preserves the car's value and extends its life by 100,000+ miles. For sub-£6,000 cars, consider a used engine or targeted repair; for £6,000-£10,000 cars, a reconditioned engine is viable; for £10,000+ cars, a rebuilt engine with warranty makes strong financial sense.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 8 Series 840Ci engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 8 Series 840Ci engine replacement takes 2-5 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The M60B40 and M62B44 are V8 engines with good engine bay access on the E31, but the job requires removing the front end and gearbox. Most specialists offer collection/delivery options nationwide with same-day dispatch available for in-stock engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 840Ci and 850Ci engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 840Ci uses a V8 engine (4.0L M60B40 or 4.4L M62B44, 286hp), while the 850Ci uses a V12 engine (5.0L M70B50 or 5.4L M73B54, 326hp). The 840Ci offers better fuel economy and lower running costs, while the 850Ci delivers more power and the unique character of a V12. The 840Ci engine replacement cost is generally lower than the 850Ci's V12.

The M60B40 and M62B44 V8s are generally robust engines, but age-related issues are now common. The M60B40 is known for timing chain tensioner wear and Nikasil cylinder lining issues on early cars. The M62B44 is prone to intake air leaks and oil leaks. Regular maintenance and early diagnosis of symptoms are key to longevity.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 8 Series 840Ci - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 840Ci joined the E31 8 Series range in 1993 as the entry-level V8 variant, positioned below the V12-powered 850Ci and 850CSi. Over its seven-year production run, the 840Ci was powered by two generations of BMW V8 - the M60B40 and the later M62B44 - offering smooth, refined V8 power in one of BMW's most iconic grand tourers.

milestones.description: M60B40, 4.0L V8, 286hp (210kW), introduced with the E31 840Ci
M62B44, 4.4L V8, 286hp (210kW), replaced M60B40 with updated engine management and improved torque
E31 8 Series production ends; the 840Ci is not carried forward to the E63 6 Series or later generations

commonProblems.h3: The BMW 8 Series 840Ci is powered by two generations of BMW V8 - the M60B40 (1993-1996) and the M62B44 (1996-1999). While these are renowned for their smooth power delivery and distinctive V8 character, age-related issues are now common on 25-32-year-old examples. Rebuilt 840Ci engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the BMW 8 Series 840Ci M60B40 Rattles
problems.rootCause: The M60B40's hydraulic timing chain tensioner can seize or lose tension. This allows the timing chain to slap against the guides, producing a rattling or grinding noise from the front of the engine, particularly on startup or at idle. If left unaddressed, chain guide failure can lead to catastrophic engine damage.

problems.h4: Intake Air Leaks - Why the BMW 8 Series 840Ci M62B44 Stalls and Idles Roughly
problems.rootCause: The M62B44's intake system is prone to air leaks from perished rubber hoses, gaskets, and the intake manifold seals. These leaks cause the engine to run lean, resulting in rough idle, stalling, hesitation on acceleration, and reduced power.
